title: Skhirat coup attempt, 10 July 1971
subtitle: During King Hassan II's 42nd birthday celebration at the royal palace in Skhirat, roughly 1,400 cadets from the Ahermoumou military school, organised by General Mohamed Medbouh, opened fire on the assembled guests. Sources consulted report roughly a hundred guests killed and about 200 wounded, alongside cadet casualties in the confusion. The king survived by hiding in a dressing-room adjoining the throne room. Seventy-four officers were later tried; ten senior officers, including four generals, were executed.

title: The Aviators' Plot — attack on Hassan II's Boeing, 16 August 1972
subtitle: Four Royal Moroccan Air Force F-5 fighters, led by Kouera el-Ouafi and organised with Kenitra air base commander Mohammed Amekrane, attacked King Hassan II's Royal Air Maroc Boeing 727 as it returned from France. Sources consulted report eight dead and dozens wounded, though accounts vary on whether these casualties came from the airborne attack, a second strafing pass at Rabat-Salé airport, or both. The king's pilot, Mohammed Kabbaj, is reported to have landed the damaged aircraft (two of three engines hit) despite a jammed wheel causing a runway excursion. Hassan II had his bodyguard broadcast a false report of his own death, which caused the attacking pilots to stand down. General Mohamed Oufkir, defence minister, is named in every source consulted as the plot's principal organiser. Amekrane fled to Gibraltar, was extradited, and was executed. Oufkir died that same evening; the official cause was suicide. Sixty detained conspirators were later transferred to Tazmamart prison in 1973, where sources report only 28 of 58 survived eighteen years of detention.
